question: How do demand and inventory policies affect prices and availability in a simulated market?
status_label: Simulation study. Preprint draft, not peer-reviewed. The frozen confirmatory matrix ran in full (925,000 simulated seasons, 0 failed). The owner's full-text review of the manuscript is pending (M6). Nothing here describes any real seller, fare or pricing system.

experiments.title: Tuned occupancy and demand-responsive rules versus the best fixed price, base scenario
experiments.verdict: H0 rejected for OCC and for DRP: both Bonferroni-adjusted 97.5% paired bootstrap intervals exclude 0, and both effects are detectable and practically relevant (SESOI 1% of FIX* revenue). The FIX6 sensitivity changes neither sign nor class, so the result is not attributed to grid resolution (a one-sided check).
notes: Selected policies: FIX(p = 139.61), OCC(p0 = 159.24, k = 4), DRP(p0 = 100.48, eta = 0.1); no tuned configuration lies on a grid edge.
n = 4,000 paired evaluation streams per contrast. Paired t intervals agree with the bootstrap intervals (manuscript Table 2).
FIX6 is FIX re-tuned on the 6 starting prices available to the rules. It is a weaker comparator by construction, so this check can only fail in one direction.

experiments.title: Sensitivity to price elasticity and demand-to-capacity tightness
experiments.verdict: 18 of 18 contrasts reject H0 after Holm adjustment (family-wise alpha 0.05); the directions are mixed: 8 negative and 10 positive. The sign is cell-specific: the rules lose in every loose-capacity cell (kappa = 1.0) and in sv1.0-k2.0.

notes: Cells: sv = valuation dispersion sigma_v, k = expected arrivals to capacity kappa; FIX re-tuned in every cell; n = 4,000 paired streams per cell; paired bootstrap 95% intervals.
Every raw sign-flip p-value is at the permutation floor 1/10001, so every Holm value (0.0018) is a bound.
8 of the 18 rule selections lie on a grid edge; under the frozen reading an upper edge may understate the rule, and the DRP lower edge does not keep prices near p0 (claim C-012).
Interaction contrasts use an independent stratified bootstrap and are descriptive.

experiments.verdict: The pre-specified invalidation rule is not triggered for OCC or DRP: at demand x0.8 and x1.25 every 95% interval of the contrast against the base-tuned FIX lies above 0, the same side as EXP-001.

notes: The policies tuned at the base cell are evaluated without re-tuning; a FIX re-tuned on each cell's own tuning streams separates the cost of misspecification from policy structure. Paired bootstrap 95% intervals, n = 4,000 per cell, descriptive.
In the reversed-arrivals cell the re-tuned fixed price is the base price, so the two comparisons coincide.
The invalidation rule compares the rules with an equally misspecified fixed price; it is weaker than a test of structural advantage.

assumptions.name: Initial stock
assumptions.value: C = 100 units; unsold units perish with zero salvage

assumptions.name: Buyer segments
assumptions.value: L (share 0.7, median valuation 100, arrives early) and H (share 0.3, median valuation 200, arrives late)

assumptions.name: Demand surges
assumptions.value: start probability 0.05 per period, length 3 periods, factor 1.8, non-compounding

assumptions.name: Buyer behaviour
assumptions.value: myopic, unit demand: a buyer buys if valuation >= price and stock remains, otherwise leaves for good

assumptions.name: Tuning budget
assumptions.value: 36 configurations per family on the same 500 tuning streams; 4,000 disjoint evaluation streams per cell

assumptions.name: Currency
assumptions.value: abstract currency units; no real prices, fares or markets

limitations: Simulation only. All data are synthetic. Results hold only within the model's assumptions and are not evidence about any real market, airline, hotel or proprietary pricing system.

Myopic, unit-demand buyers. Buyers do not wait strategically, do not return, do not compare competitors and buy at most one unit. Strategic behaviour can change optimal price paths and welfare (Su, 2007).
Monopoly, single product, no competition. No competing sellers, no product differentiation, no network of resources.

Arbitrary parameter values. Segment shares, valuation medians, shock sizes and horizons are planning choices, not calibrated estimates. EXP-002 and EXP-003 probe sensitivity but cannot cover every plausible market.
Consumer surplus is a proxy. It depends on synthetic valuations; it is not a welfare measurement of real people.
Simple policy families. Only three rule families are compared, each with a 36-configuration tuning budget; the optimal dynamic program is not part of the primary comparison.
No costs. No marginal, holding or salvage values beyond zero salvage at the deadline.
Toolchain. No TeX distribution: LaTeX output is generated but not compiled locally; PDFs come from the Typst path.
Literature search is targeted, not systematic. No novelty claim is made.

Tuning grids may bind. In the exploratory pilot (J-0003 to J-0005), the tuned DRP and OCC sensitivities sat at edges of the draft grid in every cell. The frozen v1.0 grids are wider within the same 36-configuration budget (D-009), but a tuning-only check (J-0006) still left 7 of 20 pilot optima on an edge, all in EXP-002 cells, and a DRP optimum at eta = 0 (a fixed price) in two cells. Edge optima are reported as findings under the rule of research/protocol.md section 4; where an optimum sits on an upper or price edge, the contrast measures the family as gridded.
Unspecified design details. These details are implementation choices (D-006), not empirically grounded: the arrival-profile shape, the within-period arrival order and the DRP target-rate reading.

Results are cell-specific (EXP-002, confirmatory 2026-11-25). The dynamic rules beat the tuned fixed price at the base cell (EXP-001) but lose to it in every loose-capacity cell (kappa = 1.0) and in sv1.0-k2.0. No claim of a general advantage of dynamic pricing is supported, even within the model.

Grid edges in the confirmatory tuning. 8 tuned optima in EXP-002 lie on a grid edge: DRP at eta = 0.025 in sv0.25-k1.0, sv0.5-k1.0, sv1.0-k1.0 and sv1.0-k2.0; OCC at k = 0.25 in sv0.5-k1.0 and sv1.0-k1.0; OCC at k = 8 in sv0.25-k2.0; OCC at p0 = 400 and k = 8 in sv1.0-k4.0. Under the frozen rule, lower edges are read as rules close to a fixed price; the upper and price edges mean the OCC contrast in those two cells measures the family as gridded and may understate it. No edge optimum occurred at the base cell (EXP-001, EXP-003 base tuning).

Sign-flip p-values at the permutation floor. In EXP-002 every raw p-value equals 1/10001, the smallest value 10,000 permutations can give; Holm-adjusted values (0.0018) are therefore bounds, not precise p-values.

Misspecification is one-sided. Base-tuned dynamic rules lose to the base-tuned fixed price when demand falls to 0.6 times the tuning level (EXP-003, descriptive), and against a fixed price re-tuned to the true demand they lose at x0.6 and, for OCC, at x0.8 and without shocks. The advantage depends on demand not falling far below the tuning forecast.
Shared machine. Confirmatory timings were measured with two concurrent jobs on a machine shared with other sessions.

The frozen lower-edge reading does not hold for DRP prices (M4). The protocol reads a DRP optimum at eta = 0.025 as close to a fixed price. The realised prices are not: DRP's mean price paid is 81.6 against p0 = 100.48 in sv0.5-k1.0 and 130.7 against 252.38 in sv1.0-k1.0 (research/experiments/EXP-002/arm_summary.csv). The multiplicative update compounds over 60 periods while the clearance target stays out of reach. The frozen reading is kept and this contradiction is disclosed.

Coarse starting-price grid for the rules (M4). The rules choose among 6 starting prices and FIX among 36. An exploratory, in-sample decomposition on tuning streams (J-0012, B1) attributes the OCC losses in sv0.25-k1.0 and sv1.0-k2.0 to this resolution rather than to the occupancy response. EXP-002 registered no FIX6 arm, so the frozen analysis cannot check it.

One-sided robustness checks (M4). The FIX6 check of EXP-001 could not reverse a positive result, because FIX6 chooses among a subset of FIX's prices. The EXP-003 invalidation rule compares the rules with an equally misspecified fixed price. Neither check is a strong test of structural advantage.

Tightness and price level are confounded (M4). In EXP-002, the tuned price and the purchase elasticity at that price change with kappa as well as with sigma_v (elasticity -0.955 to -2.156). The tightness pattern cannot be attributed to tightness alone.

Exploratory checks are post hoc (M4). The checks B1 to B4 (J-0012) were computed after the results were seen, are unadjusted, and B1 is in-sample on tuning streams. They qualify interpretations; they never change a frozen verdict.

Number-trace limits (M4). The automated number trace matches each displayed number to some stored value at the displayed precision. It cannot show that a number is quoted for the right quantity, and it is weak for small values. The main tables were therefore checked by key, and the prose was checked by reading (research/publication/evidence_audit.md).

exploratory_checks.title: Tuning-stream decomposition (in-sample)
exploratory_checks.verdict: Qualifies the EXP-001 gain: the rules gain despite a coarser starting-price grid.
notes: Exploratory and post hoc (journal J-0012); no simulation was run; not evidence for any preregistered hypothesis.
